title: Econometrics for finance
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Estimate and test linear regressions, handle heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation and multicollinearity, model time series with trends, AR and ARMA models, test for stationarity and unit roots, model volatility, and use panel data and event studies, in Python.
primary_reading: QuantEcon: free lectures on quantitative economics with Python

weeks.6: Time series basics: trends and seasonality
weeks.12: Machine learning and its pitfalls in finance

blocks.deliverable: Estimate and test a multiple regression on return data.
Compare ordinary and robust standard errors.
Test for a January effect with a dummy variable.
Week 7 midterm; fit an AR(1) model and forecast.
Estimate a GARCH(1,1) model on daily returns.
Run an event study around earnings announcements.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Empirical study: choose a testable question about markets (for example whether earnings surprises move prices), gather or use supplied data, estimate the model in Python with diagnostics, and write a five-page paper with results, robustness checks and limitations.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
